marks.gloss_en: אלמא איסור מוקדשין קדים -- inferred from R' Yochanan's nefel whose limbs exist before its sinews
evidently the prohibition of consecrated meat comes first
דתניא: והקטיר הכהן את הכל ... מחוברין יעלו, פרשו ירדו
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: they disagree about bringing it up [to the altar]
רבי היא, דתניא ... רבי אומר: ... מחוברין יעלו, פרשו אפילו בראשו של מזבח ירדו
the tanna who says 'detached, they descend' is Rebbi
אף על גב דאיסור מוקדשין קדים, אתי איסור גיד חייל עלייהו, שכן איסורו נוהג בבני נח (= p_gid_chal_bnei_noach)
even though the prohibition of consecrated meat comes first, the nerve's prohibition comes and takes effect on them, since its prohibition applies to the sons of Noach
מאן שמעת ליה האי סברא? רבי יהודה; והא מתניתין דלא כרבי יהודה, דקתני נוהג ... בירך של ימין ובירך של שמאל
the one known to hold this reasoning is R' Yehuda
האי תנא סבר לה כוותיה בחדא, ופליג עליה בחדא (= p_kevateih_bachada)
this tanna holds like him [R' Yehuda] in one matter and disputes him in one
אימר דשמעת ליה לרבי יהודה בטמאה דאיסור לאו, קדשים דאיסור כרת -- מי שמעת ליה? -- unanswered; the stam turns to אלא at 90a.6
rather, here [the clause] deals with an animal giving birth to its firstborn, which is holy at the womb
and if you wish say: the offspring of consecrated animals are holy [only] at their coming into being
R' Chiya bar Yosef: [the mishna] taught only kodashim that are eaten; with kodashim that are not eaten the nerve's prohibition does not apply
Rav Pappa: they do not disagree -- here as to flogging him, there as to bringing it up [to the altar]
Rav Pappa (other version): they do not disagree -- here as to removing it, there as to bringing it up
the first tanna: 'the flesh and the blood' is fulfilled with what springs off [the fire] -- partly-consumed flesh you return, partly-consumed sinews and bones you do not
Rebbi: one verse includes, one verse excludes; how so? attached, they ascend; detached, even at the top of the altar, they descend
the Rabbis: for attached parts no verse was needed to include them, as with the head of a burnt-offering; the verse was needed for detached ones
Rebbi: attached permitted parts needed no verse to include them; the verse was needed for the sciatic nerve while attached
